gen.title: How changing war aims transformed the war
gen.orderNote: Follow how changing war aims led to a limited military action that transformed the war

steps.label: preserve the Union
steps.quote: Initially, the Civil War between North and South was fought by the North to prevent the secession of the Southern states and preserve the Union.
steps.orderHint: Start with the initial cause before change

steps.label: Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation
steps.quote: That changed on September 22, 1862, when President Lincoln issued his Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation
steps.orderHint: This warning comes next in the source

steps.label: military measure
steps.quote: Because it was a military measure, however, the Emancipation Proclamation was limited in many ways.
steps.orderHint: This explains why the next limit followed

steps.label: loyal border states
steps.quote: It applied only to states that had seceded from the Union, leaving slavery untouched in the loyal border states.

steps.label: transform the character of the war
steps.quote: Although the Emancipation Proclamation did not end slavery in the nation, it did fundamentally transform the character of the war.
steps.orderHint: This effect follows the limited action

steps.label: acceptance of Black men into the Union Army and Navy
steps.quote: Moreover, the Proclamation announced the acceptance of Black men into the Union Army and Navy, enabling the liberated to become liberators.
steps.orderHint: This final result expands the domain of freedom
